title: Early forms of Governm ent in Kenya
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 5 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Facts (to confirm): Maasai laibon, age-sets and morans; Ameru Njuri Ncheke and the Mugwe; Agikuyu kiama; Wanga kingdom under the Nabongo.

skills.key_step: The child describes early forms of government in Kenya (councils of elders, age-sets, spiritual leaders, clan heads, the Wanga king).

floor.prerequisite: Names community leaders and their duties.
floor.question: What do elders do?

representations: a chart of communities and their governments
a story of a council meeting
steps: Say whether it had a king.

board.do: Write council of elders, age-set, king.

board.say: Which Kenyan community had a king?

board.do: Write a community beside each form.

misconceptions.ask: How were communities governed before colonial rule?
misconceptions.repair: Ask who settled disputes and made rules in a village before colonial rule.

misconceptions.ask: Which of these communities was ruled by a king?
misconceptions.repair: Compare the Wanga kingdom with the council-ruled Ameru.
Compare: your class learns together; an age-set had duties together, like defending the community.

misconceptions.ask: Which Kenyan community had a king?
misconceptions.repair: Show Mumias and the Nabongo title.

checks.question: Did Kenyan communities have government before colonial rule?
checks.answer: Yes, councils of elders, age-sets and some kings

checks.question: What was an age-set?
checks.answer: a group initiated at the same time with duties for their age

skills.key_step: The child compares Maasai and Ameru early government: both used councils of elders and age-sets; the Maasai had the laibon and the morans, the Ameru the Njuri Ncheke and the Mugwe.

floor.question: Name one early form of government.
floor.answer: any form such as a council of elders

representations: a picture of morans and elders
steps: Place the shared parts: elders and age-sets.
Place the titles: laibon and morans; Njuri Ncheke and Mugwe.
contexts: the Njuri Ncheke shrine in Meru

board.do: Draw two columns: Maasai and Ameru.

board.say: What was their council of elders called?

misconceptions.ask: What was the council of elders of the Ameru called?
misconceptions.repair: Link the Maasai laibon to the spiritual leader and the Njuri Ncheke to the Ameru elders.

listen_for: He ruled alone as a king
misconceptions.ask: How was the Maasai laibon different from a king?
misconceptions.repair: Ask who made decisions about cattle raids and grazing.

misconceptions.ask: What was the main duty of Maasai morans?
misconceptions.repair: Sort duties: elders decided, morans defended, the laibon guided.

misconceptions.ask: What did the Njuri Ncheke do?
misconceptions.repair: Read a short story of the council settling a land case.

checks.question: What was the spiritual leader of the Maasai called?
What was the council of elders of the Ameru called?

skills.key_step: The child picks good practices from early government and links each to today.

floor.question: What did a council of elders do?

representations: practice and today cards to pair
steps: Ask: is it still good today?
Find the modern practice like it.

board.do: Write: "elders asked the community before deciding".

board.say: What do we call this in government today?

misconceptions.ask: Which practice from early government is still useful today?
misconceptions.repair: Match each old practice to a modern office.

misconceptions.ask: Which old practice should NOT be copied today?
misconceptions.repair: Sort practices into keep and leave behind with reasons.

misconceptions.ask: Elders settled quarrels by listening to both sides. Which modern practice is like this?
misconceptions.repair: Match practice and today in pairs on the board.

misconceptions.ask: Which duty did young people have in many early Kenyan communities?
misconceptions.repair: Link age-set duties to youth service and youth leaders today.

checks.question: Give one good practice from early government that is used today.
checks.answer: any of: consulting elders, settling quarrels by talk, leaders serving the people, duties for youth

checks.question: Should harsh punishments from long ago be used today?
checks.answer: No; only good practices that respect rights
